messages:
amanda: heads up — after last night's LDAP attr rename i see multiple services lost 'owner' bindings. lots of role_bindings pointing at extid ldap:team-ops:742 which doesn't exist in SCIM anymore. any ideas? :frowning:
jc: hmm, looks like the migration script renamed `team_ops` -> `team-ops` but our SCIM extId normalization expects the old prefix. could be a canonicalization mismatch. did the scim-provisioner run after the migration?
deploy-bot: scim-sync job 1953456120 finished — status: partial
  summary: 120 groups processed, 1 failed, 5 warnings
  failed_groups: ["ldap:team-ops:742"]
  error: "extId not found in mapping table"
mike_sre: that's the one. the role_binding rows still point to the old extid string that the runtime uses to resolve group -> role. if SCIM removed the group we end up with orphaned role_bindings which look like privileged users lost access.
ria_sec: ok step 1: don't mass-change bindings yet. step 2: run audit query to list all role_bindings with missing group refs and capture affected principals. run:```sql
SELECT rb.id, rb.role, rb.target_extid, u.email
FROM role_bindings rb
LEFT JOIN scim_groups g ON rb.target_extid = g.extid
LEFT JOIN users u ON rb.principal_id = u.id
WHERE g.id IS NULL;
```
amanda: running it now. also checking audit logs to see when the extid was removed from SCIM.
amanda: result (snippet):
```
id: 8941, role: owner, target_extid: ldap:team-ops:742, email: john.doe@redwood.com
id: 8942, role: owner, target_extid: ldap:team-ops:742, email: svc-deploy@redwood.com
```
jc: john.doe is expected. that's bad — his owner access got orphaned. can we map extid -> new group name? maybe the migration renamed it to ldap:team_ops:742 or ldap:team-ops:742? check SCIM history.
mike_sre: i pulled SCIM event: group create (2026-03-18T03:12Z) extId: "ldap:team_ops:742" (underscore). the provisioning script later normalized to hyphen for some services but not all. we have a split mapping.
ria_sec: options: 1) re-insert a synthetic SCIM group with the old extid (temporary) to reattach bindings, then run a clean migration that updates bindings to the canonical extid; 2) update role_bindings rows to point at the new extid and record change in audit log; 3) run the reconcile tool to nuke stale bindings after owner revalidation. i prefer option 1 for minimizing downtime while we validate.
amanda: if we create a synthetic group, we'll need to ensure KMS policies don't accidentally grant secrets to a placeholder group. anyone aware of KMS key grants tied to group ids?
mike_sre: yes — the kms-roles table references scim_group_id for a few encryption keys (mostly infra). quick check:```sql
SELECT key_id FROM kms_roles WHERE scim_group_extid = 'ldap:team-ops:742';
```
amanda: returns one key: key-analytics-prod. that's sensitive. we should not blindly reattach without confirming current membership.
jc: safe path: create synthetic group with extid and mark it as 'reconciliation-temp' and set membership to current members of the new canonical group, then rotate KMS grant to reference the synthetic group only after verification. also ensure audit_log entries note the synthetic creation.
ria_sec: i'll open an audit ticket and annotate the db changes. runbooks: call out to security review and record decision. for rollback: we can drop synthetic group and restore old bindings from a DB snapshot.
amanda: i'll provision the synthetic group now in staging and run a dry-run of the binding remap script: `scim-repair --from-extid ldap:team-ops:742 --to-extid ldap:team_ops:742 --dry-run`.
amanda: dry-run output: 2 role_bindings would be remapped, 1 kms grant would be updated (dry-run: no change applied).
mike_sre: once you confirm dry-run, run it with `--apply` during a maintenance window and follow the playbook. i'll coordinate KMS ACLs and review key policies.
oncall-bot: paging oncall (mike_sre) — new security reconciliation in progress. :pager:
ria_sec: post-action: we should add a normalization test to our SCIM unit tests to prevent future extid shape drift, and add a short-lived alert when scim-sync reports partial failures. noted in backlog ticket SEC-4521.
amanda: thanks all. i'll schedule the apply for 0200 UTC and post updates here. :thumbsup:
